subject: Small sample sizes and few site visits in occupancy modelling

messages.author: 77e0f8e9f257430f
messages.subject: Small sample sizes and few site visits in occupancy modelling
parts:
Hi! I'm working with point count bird data, right now I'm trying to learn single season-single species modelling. So each point count-site was visited only twice in one season (and some only once, due to weather problems and such). So of what I understand, for this reason it is important to check that the estimated detection probability is not under 0.15 (I found this recommendation in MackKenzie et al. 2002). How do I get this estimate? Is it with the function backTransform(linearComb(detectionmodel, coefficients=c(?,?), type="det"))? In that case, how do I know what values to put in the coefficients=c() part? I tried looking for help in R but I can't find any instructions for the function.

Second: If I understand correctly, AICc is used to correct for small sample sizes. What is a small sample size, in an occupancy modelling context? And let's say my sample size is small. How do I get the AICc? When I use the modSel() function, I don't seem to get that info in the output. Or is it called something else?

Thanks!
